item.title: About
item.author: kasadasasha@gmail.com (Sasha Casada)
item.description:
Server-side engineer based in Tokyo. Lover of mirth and gaiety.

My focus is on distributed systems, multiplayer networking, and cloud infrastructure. I primarily work with Go, C, Kubernetes, and Terraform.

I studied Computer Science and Japanese at Swarthmore College, and spent time studying at The University of Tokyo. During my time at Swarthmore, I worked as a project manager and was on the board of the Swarthmore College Computer Society (SCCS).

item.title: Zero-Allocation Logging in Go
item.author: kasadasasha@gmail.com (Sasha Casada)
item.description:
Go Zero-Allocation Logging Under the Hood

Go’s structured logging library (log/slog), although maybe kind of boring at first glance, is a really quite clever piece of standard library code. That is: if you dive into how exactly they are able to process log attributes with zero heap allocations. Although the solution (which was inspired by the uber-go/zap and rs/zerolog packages), and this way of using the log/slog.Logger is usually not that important for generic logging use-cases, it is extremely well-optimized for any hot-path application.
